R.'''" '''Giddens''' (born February 13, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He was selected to the 2003 [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American team]], then initially played for the [[University of Kansas]] but transferred to the [[University of New Mexico]] following his sophomore season. He was selected with the 30th overall pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]], and played for various professional teams until 2019. Giddens is the former head coach of the women's basketball team at [[Northern New Mexico College]].{{cite news |url=https://www.riograndesun.com/sports/j-r-giddens-out-at-northern/article_b70913e2-c36e-11ed-9e76-333dd518f241.html |title=J.R. Giddens Out at Northern |first=Ari |last=Levin |website=iograndesun.com |date=March 15, 2023 |accessdate=June 20, 2024}} ==College== Giddens accepted a scholarship offer from University of Kansas from then-head coach [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]]. After Williams left, Giddens was persuaded to stay by Williams' replacement [[Bill Self]]. In his first year at Kansas, Giddens earned All-[[Big 12 Conference]] Freshman honors while averaging 11 [[Point (basketball)|points]] per game. In May 2005 he was involved in a fight outside a bar in Lawrence and received a stab wound. He was later charged with battery for his role in the incident and left Kansas in a mutual agreement with Self.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2147032 Ex-Jayhawk Giddens charged with battery – Men's College Basketball – ESPN]Mark Murphy, [http://www.bostonherald.com/sports/basketball/celtics/view/2008_06_26_Bulls_take_Rose_with_No__1_pick_in_NBA_draft/srvc=celt&position=4 Celtics select J.R. Giddens with 30th pick in NBA draft], ''[[Boston Herald]]'', June 27, 2008. Giddens transferred to [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico]] and sat out the next season due to [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] regulations. As a junior, he was suspended from the team in late February for disciplinary reasons and missed the team's summer trip to work on his academics.Geoff Grammer, [http://www.abqjournal.com/242050/sports/alfords-legacy-is-up-in-the-air.html ''Steve Alford: A bitter departure''], Albuquerque Journal, August 4, 2013. New Mexico hired head coach [[Steve Alford]], who took a no-nonsense approach to discipline, and Giddens made a dramatic transformation.Richard Stevens, [http://www.golobos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=26000&ATCLID=209057524&SPID=87115&SPSID=616934 ''Alford Takes UNM To New Levels, But No Sweet 16 Trip''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140320125159/http://www.golobos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209057524&SPSID=616934&SPID=87115&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=26000 |date=March 20, 2014 }}, New Mexico Athletics, June 22, 2013. As a senior, he was named [[Mountain West Conference]] Co-Player of the Year and Honorable Mention [[All-American]] following career highs in points (16.3 per game) and [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] (8.8 per game).J.R. Giddens, [http://www.golobos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=26000&ATCLID=209088587 Profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140319192344/http://www.golobos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=26000&ATCLID=209088587 |date=March 19, 2014 }}, New Mexico Athletics. ==Professional career== On June 26, 2008, Giddens was selected by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the 30th overall pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. He had worked out with the Celtics for three days, and received praises from head coach [[Doc Rivers]],Steve Bulpett, [http://www.bostonherald.com/sports/basketball/celtics/view/2008_06_27_For_Celts__future_is_now:_Giddens_pick_nice_present_for_Doc/srvc=celt&position=6 For Celts, future is now], ''[[Boston Herald]]'', June 27, 2008. who thought he could fight for minutes on the team right away.Julian Benbow, [http://archive.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/articles/2008/06/27/taking_a_shot_with_jr/ Taking a shot with J.R.], ''[[The Boston Globe]]'', June 27, 2008. He was even mentioned as a possible replacement for [[Free agent#Restricted and unrestricted free agency|restricted free agent]] [[Tony Allen (basketball)|Tony Allen]].Steve Bulpett, [http://www.bostonherald.com/sports/basketball/celtics/view/2008_06_28_Celts_drafting_offseason_plan/srvc=celt&position=3 Celts drafting offseason plan], ''[[Boston Herald]]'', June 28, 2008. Giddens was already familiar with [[Leon Powe]] and [[Kendrick Perkins]], who were his teammates at the 2003 [[McDonald's All-American Team|McDonald's All-American]] Game. But on behalf of his agent Aaron Mintz, Giddens declined to work out at the Celtics' minicamp in early July, because he had not signed a contract yet.Monique Walker, [https://web.archive.org/web/20080706171826/http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/articles/2008/07/03/this_year_davis_not_one_of_the_babies_in_camp/?page=2 This year, Davis not one of the babies in camp], ''[[The Boston Globe]]'', July 3, 2008.Scott Souza, [http://www.metrowestdailynews.com/sports/x875596005/Celtics-Giddens-a-no-show-at-mini-camp Celtics: Giddens a no-show at mini-camp], ''[[The MetroWest Daily News]]'', July 2, 2008. On November 15, 2008, Giddens was assigned to the Boston Celtics' [[NBA Development League]] affiliate team, the [[Utah Flash]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20090308062504/http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press111508-giddens-flash.html Celtics Assign Giddens to Utah Flash | Celtics.com] He had played with the Celtics in the [[2008–09 NBA season|2008–09]] pre-season but had been on the inactive list for the first 10 games of the regular season. He was recalled by the Celtics from Utah Flash development team on February 8, 2009.{{Cite web |url=http://scores.heraldinteractive.com/merge/tsnform.aspx?c=bostonherald&page=nba%2Fteams%2F092%2Fteam.aspx%3Fid%3D092 |title=Boston Celtics player transactions (Boston Herald) |access-date=January 28, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110510020710/http://scores.heraldinteractive.com/merge/tsnform.aspx?c=bostonherald&page=nba%2Fteams%2F092%2Fteam.aspx%3Fid%3D092 |archive-date=May 10, 2011 |url-status=dead }} Giddens started his first game for the Boston Celtics on January 2, 2010. On February 18, 2010, Giddens, [[Bill Walker (basketball)|Bill Walker]] and [[Eddie House]] were traded to the [[New York Knicks]] for [[Nate Robinson]] and [[Marcus Landry]].{{cite web|title=Knicks Acquire Eddie House, J.R. Giddens and Bill Walker |work=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/news/celtics_trade1002.html |date=February 18, 2010 |access-date=March 12, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100221041057/http://www.nba.com/knicks/news/celtics_trade1002.html |archive-date=February 21, 2010 }} On October 13, 2010, Giddens's agent said that Giddens would spend the 2010–11 season with [[Asseco Prokom Gdynia]] in [[Poland]],[https://web.archive.org/web/20110722122603/http://www.kob.com/article/stories/S1790458.shtml?cat=502 Giddens to play in Europe] but Giddens left the team in December 2010 by mutual consent.{{Cite web |url=http://www.asseco.prokom.pl/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=940:kontrakt-z-jr-giddensem-rozwizany-za-porozumieniem&catid=11:aktualnosci&Itemid=54&lang=en |title=JR Giddens leaves Prokom |access-date=December 31, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120313200537/http://www.asseco.prokom.pl/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=940:kontrakt-z-jr-giddensem-rozwizany-za-porozumieniem&catid=11:aktualnosci&Itemid=54&lang=en |archive-date=March 13, 2012 |url-status=dead }} In September 2011, Giddens signed with [[PAOK Thessaloniki]] of Greece.[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/87446/180 PAOK signs swingman Giddens] In September 2012, Giddens signed with [[Basket Brescia Leonessa]], an Italian Legadue team. On June 30, 2014, he signed with [[Vaqueros de Bayamón]] of Puerto Rico.{{cite news|title=JR Giddens inks with Vaqueros de Bayamon|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/124957/jg-giddens-inks-with-vaqueros-de-bayamon.html|access-date=June 30, 2014|work=Sportando.com}} On November 22, 2014, Giddens signed with [[Peñarol de Mar del Plata]] of Argentina.{{cite news|title=J.R. Giddens (ex Bayamon) agreed terms with Penarol|url=http://www.latinbasket.com/Argentina/news/384103/J.R.-Giddens-%28ex-Bayamon%29-agreed-terms-with-Penarol|access-date=November 22, 2014|work=Eurobasket.com|date=November 22, 2014}} On March 10, 2015, he was waived by the Peñarol after appearing in seventeen [[Liga Nacional de Básquet|LNB]] games.{{cite news|title=Penarol cut J.R. Giddens|url=http://www.latinbasket.com/Argentina/news/397612/Penarol-cut-J.R.-Giddens|access-date=March 12, 2015|work=Eurobasket.com|date=March 10, 2015}} In January 2017, Giddens signed with [[Club Trouville]] of the [[Liga Uruguaya de Basketball]].[http://www.latinbasket.com/Uruguay/news/475676/Trouville-lands-J.R.-Giddens,-ex-Leones-SD Trouville lands J.R. Giddens, ex Leones SD] The next month, he left the club after appearing in five games.[http://www.ovaciondigital.com.uy/basquetbol/basquetbol-trouville-super-liga.html Trouville y un nuevo recambio] {{in lang|es}} On February 22, 2017, he signed with Mexican club Mineros de Parral.[https://www.facebook.com/minerosdeparralbasketbol/photos/pcb.1815676122014884/1815675162014980/?type=3&theater Te presentamos a los nuevos refuerzos del equipo mineros de parral, de excelente nivel, el orgullo parralense y jugador reconocido en liga nacional Alan Olivas, así como el jugador ex NBA (knicks-celtics) JR Giddens] {{in lang|es}} On March 22, 2018, Giddens signed with [[Ferro Carril Oeste (basketball)|Ferro Carril Oeste]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Básquet]] in [[Argentina]].{{cite web|website=sportando.com|date=March 22, 2018|access-date=March 24, 2018|author=Cauchi, O.|title=J.R. Giddens inks with Ferro Basquet|url=https://sportando.basketball/m/en/america/argentine/268864/jr-giddens-inks-with-ferro-basquet.html}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ==Stabbing incident== On May 19, 2005, Giddens was stabbed in his right calf in a bar fight in [[Lawrence, Kansas]], requiring 30 stitches.{{Cite web |url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/J.R.-Giddens-74/ |title=DraftExpress.com NBA Draft Prospect Profile: J.R. Giddens |access-date=June 27, 2008 |archive-date=June 8, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230608080131/http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/J.R.-Giddens-74/ |url-status=dead }} ==Personal== * [[Academic major|Majored]] in university studies. *Cleared {{height|ft=6|in=10}} as a high jumper in high school. *His parents are Charles and Dianna, and he has two sisters, Breeanna and Portia. *Lists [[Steve Urkel]] and [[Mr. Rogers]] as his favorite television characters. * Has sixteen tattoos, including his first initial "J" on his left triceps and his last initial "G" on his right triceps, and the [[Bible]] verse [[Philippians]] 4:13 – ''"I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength"'' – on his right shoulder.Jeremy Fowler, [http://www.abqtrib.com/news/2007/feb/10/mens-basketball-lobo-jr-giddens-seeks-rise-above-l/ Men's basketball: Lobo J.R.
